column3: 12 V 7 Ah sealed lead-acid with F1 terminals (ExpertPower EXP1270 or equivalent)
column10: One battery runs the robot; a second in parallel adds capacity, not voltage. Retail range from ExpertPower direct to eBay.

column3: Cen-Tech 12 V 2 A SLA charger (Harbor Freight)
column10: Carried over from the old master BOM; price not re-checked.

column10: Carried over from the old master BOM.
This is the pack the robot was tested with. Most retailers $119-137. Skip this line if you already own one.
MSRP about $169; $100 was a sale price. Not run on the robot yet.

column3: Printed pack receiver with metal contacts and a lead to the robot
column10: Not priced. Contacts must be metal; do not rely on printed plastic to carry current.

column3: 12.8 V 10 Ah LiFePO4 with 10 A BMS (typical Amazon listing)
column10: A 10 A BMS is probably too small for four RS550 motors and may trip under load. Prefer a BMS rated for the robot's real peak current.

column3: 12.8 V 20 Ah LiFePO4 with 20 A BMS
column10: Range runs from budget brands to ExpertPower at the top. Still a 20 A BMS; peak current not yet measured.

column3: LiFePO4 charger matched to the pack
column10: Not priced. Do not use an SLA float charger.

column3: F1 or the battery's own terminal type
column10: Check the pack's terminals before buying.
